correctness.rationale: The displayed C is the cumulative candidate; its survival term is exp(−x−y−t) with x=−log(1−u), y=−log(1−v), t=φx^a y^b. The exponential correction is bounded by (1−u)(1−v), giving continuity even at the unit sides; the other sides are grounded and both margins are uniform. The interior mixed derivative has sign of H=(x+at)(y+bt)−ab t, by the chain rule. A negative interior value violates two-increasingness on a small rectangle; a nonnegative interior derivative extends the rectangle inequalities to the boundary by continuity. If a<1, fix 0<y<b; x^(−a)H→φa y^b(y−b)<0 for every positive φ, and the same argument with coordinates exchanged excludes b<1. For a,b≥1 and φ>0, set r=x/(at), s=y/(bt), m=a+b−1. The inverse is t=(φa^a b^b r^a s^b)^(−1/m), x=art, y=bst, onto the whole positive quadrant. The sign restriction becomes φ≤(1+r)^m(1+s)^m/(a^a b^b r^a s^b) for every r,s>0. Each one-variable minimum is global, at r=a/(b−1) and s=b/(a−1) when the denominators are positive and at the corresponding infinity limit otherwise. Multiplication yields exactly Φ. Equality is allowed whether or not the infimum is attained; any strict violation admits finite positive r,s with negative density. At φ=0 the candidate is uv without exponent restrictions. I checked Φ(1,3)=1/4 and verified by exact fractions H(4/9,4/9)=0 at (a,b,φ)=(2,2,729/256) versus −37232/4782969 at φ=3. A half-power witness gives H=−4573/8000000 at (a,b,φ,x,y)=(1/2,1,1/2,1/10000,1/2).
residual_risks: The rational witnesses check selected equalities/signs, not continuum sufficiency. This is a validity theorem for finite parameters, not an estimation, sampling or model-fit result.

value.rationale: The candidate was introduced as a model for bivariate failures. Nonnegative rectangle probabilities are a prerequisite before fitting or interpreting it.
